name: Digital Lending — Prohibited Pool/Pass-Through Account Pattern
sourceDocument: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
referenceNumber: not independently confirmed — RBI's notification PDF is CAPTCHA-gated and could not be fetched directly during this research pass
confidenceNote: This document and provision consolidate and replace the September 2, 2022 Guidelines on Digital Lending, Para 3 ('Loan Disbursal, Servicing and Repayment'), which contained the equivalent prohibition. The Para 9 numbering in the 2025 Directions comes from a single secondary legal-analysis source (Synergia Legal), cross-validated against two independently-sourced paragraph numbers elsewhere in the same document (Para 6 — multi-lender arrangements; Para 17 — DLA/CIMS reporting — both confirmed by separate independent sources). This raises confidence above a single unverified claim, but the paragraph number has not been confirmed against RBI's primary PDF text directly. Verify against the primary source before citing this section number in any external-facing submission material.
clauseText: Loan disbursal and repayment must be executed directly between the borrower's bank account and the Regulated Entity's (RE) bank account, without routing through any pass-through or pool account of a Lending Service Provider (LSP) or any other third party, except for disbursals covered exclusively under statutory or regulatory mandate, flow of money between REs for co-lending transactions, or disbursals for specific end-use paid directly to the end-beneficiary's account.
observableGraphCondition: Any MoneyEdge with mechanism=POOL_PASS_THROUGH in the proposed graph.
implementationNotes: POOL_PASS_THROUGH mechanism value is set by the deterministic extractor only when evidence clearly indicates funds flowing through a third-party pool/treasury account before reaching the final destination.
This rule does NOT attempt to determine whether the overall product is a lending product — that is established by graph context (presence of FINANCING_PROVIDER actors and Obligation objects).

The regulatory exceptions listed in clauseText (statutory mandate, co-lending, specific end-use) are not handled by this rule and would require manual review if applicable — this rule is intentionally over-inclusive rather than attempting to encode the exceptions, per the project's principle that REVIEW/BLOCK on uncertainty is safer than a false PASS.
